title: How the Hoover Dam Works, Part I
summary: Hosts Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant open with personal memories of visiting Hoover Dam and a shout-out to writer Julia Layton, then cover the dam's origins: the Colorado River's flooding, the choice of Black Canyon over Boulder Canyon, the Colorado River Compact, and Herbert Hoover's role. They discuss the federal Bureau of Reclamation, the six-company construction consortium and its bid, the company town of Boulder City, and the infrastructure built before construction. Further segments cover diverting the river through four tunnels with cofferdams, smoothing canyon walls with high scalers, the dangerous work and worker deaths, the Burl Rutledge fall, and the concrete pouring and cooling methods. The episode is Part I and ends by deciding to split the topic into two parts and skipping listener mail.
topics: Hoover Dam urban legend bodies in concrete

segments.title: Opening banter and personal Hoover Dam visits
segments.summary: Hosts recall past visits to Hoover Dam, mention writer Julia Layton, and banter about Las Vegas history and Bugsy Siegel and Warren Beatty.

segments.title: Origins: Colorado River floods and choosing the dam site
segments.summary: The dam was conceived to control Colorado River flooding, provide drought water storage, and generate power. The site moved from Boulder Canyon to Black Canyon, and Herbert Hoover promoted the project.

segments.title: Federal involvement and the Colorado River Compact
segments.summary: Earlier irrigation attempts failed, the federal government stepped in, and states feared water would be diverted to California. Hoover brokered the Colorado River Compact to distribute water among the seven states.

segments.title: Naming, Hoover's unpopularity, and the six companies consortium
segments.summary: The dam was congressionally approved and renamed several times. Hoover became unpopular during the Depression. Six construction firms formed the Six Companies consortium, with a bid of about 48.8 million dollars.

segments.title: Building Boulder City and infrastructure
segments.summary: Workers' town Boulder City was built about six miles away with cottages, dormitories, and services. It was government-run until 1959 and later incorporated; the project also required highways, railways, and power lines.

segments.title: Diverting the Colorado River through tunnels
segments.summary: Engineers built cofferdams and four diversion tunnels, each about a mile long and lined with concrete, to route the river around the construction site.

segments.title: High scalers, dangerous work, and hard hats
segments.summary: Canyon walls were smoothed by high scalers working on ropes. Workers lacked hard hats until a strike, and they made hard boiled hats from coal tar. The Burl Rutledge fall and rescue by Oliver Cowen and Arnold Parks are described.

segments.title: Worker deaths, heat, and the body-in-concrete myth
segments.summary: Roughly 96 to 112 deaths are estimated, with pneumonia and carbon monoxide as possible causes, and heat stroke was common. The hosts say the urban legend about bodies in the concrete is false.

segments.title: Gravity arch design and concrete pouring
segments.summary: The gravity arch design uses water and canyon walls to strengthen the dam. Concrete was poured in blocks and cooled with internal steel pipes, and grout filled the cracks. The episode ends with a decision to split it into two parts.
